A.question: Under incomplete observed contact/acceptance graphs, is the maximum cardinality of mutually accepting bipartite pairings point-identified? Derive and empirically exercise sharp worst-case bounds rather than silently filling in invisible contacts.
A.estimand: For an n by n finite at-risk bipartite market, K(G)=maximum matching cardinality in complete latent graph of bilateral yes/yes. Observed records fix bilateral outcomes only on actual encounters. Identified set is [K(E_observed_mutual), K(E_observed_mutual ∪ E_unobserved)] under only binary completion of unobserved dyads.
A.units: 504 independent simulated markets, not humans; 9 female-side and 9 male-side agents with at most 81 possible pair encounters
A.outcome: Interval endpoints L,U; latent K only for simulator audit; observed dyadic yes/no and exposure matrix
A.scope: Assumes all cross-side dyads feasible, no capacity beyond one partner, observed no must stay no; no timing or persistence.

B.preferred: Incomplete encounter networks frequently leave a non-singleton identified set for latent attainable mutual matches.
B.null: With sufficient observed exposures L=U or observed outcomes alone identify K, even without all dyads encountered.
rivals: Model-based MAR imputation would yield a point under untestable assumptions
Structural institutional constraints might shrink the unknown possible-edge set
No independent original 2-vote longitudinal human record yet qualifies R5
B.status: Exploratory synthetic methodology; already strong prior art from Manski 2005 and Horowitz/Manski 2006; do not claim novelty of generic partial identification.

C.treatment: Three exposure mechanisms MCAR, actor-specific selection, and outcome-dependent MNAR at each of four exposure rates 0.15,0.35,0.60,0.85, 40 independent pre-set seeds per cell; plus 8 complete-exposure null controls per mechanism.
C.comparators: Actual latent complete matching (oracle-only, not available empirically); observed-only matching L; unconstrained completion matching U; independent Python exact subset DP against JavaScript augmenting-path algorithm.
C.primary_acceptance: 504/504 all L <= latent K <= U; Python independently computes exact L,U,K for all rows; complete observation returns L=K=U for 24 null cases; manually constructed n4 observational-equivalence example gives lower0 upper4.
C.secondary: Descriptive mean bound width and point-identified fraction by exposure regime; no inferential p-values, no claims of population-specific prediction.
falsifiers: Any L>K, K>U, negative width or bound >9
Disagreement of Python subset DP and JavaScript augmenting matching
Any full-observation control fails to collapse
A silent generated-seed drift or input not reproducible

D.generator: Xorshift32 deterministic seeded 359000+mode*10000+rate*1000+repetition, all modes/rates enumerated; 24 full controls at seeds 459000+mode*100+rep; no hyperparameter fitting after outcome.
D.data: Fresh synthetic outcomes and opportunities, not human SRC104/SRC119 or any historical trajectories.

E.seed_policy: No post hoc adaptation, no reuse of 60 historical worlds or N351-N355 fixed simulated worlds; 1 cycle for all 504 worlds.

adversarial: manually chosen n4 diagonal observed negative, off-diagonal unknown, same observed data compatible with K=0 and K=4
24 complete-exposure null cases across three exposure regimes
Python subset-state DP algorithm independent from JS augmenting paths
two deliberate corruptions of manual low/high endpoints must be rejected
